findings.desc: CHK-003:adversarial:2 verificationEvidence is mis-bound: the intent claims 'An attacker adding a 15th key to the snapshot object after resolution -> the snapshot type/validator rejects or the digest changes', but the bound command (node dist/tasks/red-evidence-policy-canon-smoke.js, cited smoke:171+103) only exercises unknown-key REJECTION on the INPUT config before resolution, never on the OUTPUT snapshot after resolveRedEvidencePolicy() returns. Live re-test proves the literal claim is false: policy.ts:348-363 returns a plain (non-frozen) snapshot object; `r.snapshot.evil15thKey = "injected"` after a successful resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["/usr/bin"]}) silently succeeds (object now has 15 keys) with NO throw/rejection and the already-computed policyDigest field is unchanged (stale, not recomputed) -- neither of the intent's two disjuncts (reject | digest changes) holds. The evidence note conflates pre-resolution config-key validation (real, correctly tested elsewhere by CHK-003:adversarial:0) with post-resolution snapshot-mutation protection (untested, and demonstrably absent). Fix: either add Object.freeze(snapshot) before returning + a real test asserting the mutation throws, or reword/retire the intent to match what is actually guaranteed (input-side unknown-key rejection only).

packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/canon.ts:67-73 canon() types its parameter as `unknown` (not the exported CanonValue type) and only guards typeof===object via `if (t==="object")` -> Object.keys(obj).sort() with NO isPlainObject check, so any non-array object (Date, Map, Set, RegExp, class instance, Buffer, Error) silently falls through instead of throwing. Concrete repro: canon({createdAt:new Date("2020-01-01"),name:"x"}) === canon({createdAt:new Date("2099-12-31"),name:"x"}) === {"createdAt":{},"name":"x"} -- canonDigest of these two materially DIFFERENT records is IDENTICAL because Object.keys(dateInstance) is empty, silently collapsing the date to {}. canon(new Map([["a",1]])) also silently returns "{}". This directly contradicts the moduleuxe2x80x99s own documented contract (canon.ts:50-52: undefined/function/symbol are programming errors and THROW) which implies non-CanonValue inputs should fail loudly, and undermines the header comment/spec assurance-tier claim (canon.ts:19-21, spec S:0.6) that CANON detects accidental substitution/casual drift -- an accidental `new Date()` instead of `.toISOString()` (a very common JS mistake, and createdAt is a named field in the spec S:1.10 record schema at line 694) is exactly the class of accident S0.6 says this subsystem defends against, yet it is silently swallowed into a digest collision rather than caught. No current caller in this story passes such a value (policy.ts only builds number/string/array/plain-object fields), so it is not exploitable today, but canon() is documented as the single reused digest primitive for the whole RED-evidence subsystem (canon.ts:1-2, S:0.4) and future records (envelope/runner/receipt work) are very likely to carry timestamp fields. Fix: add an isPlainObject-style guard (Object.getPrototypeOf(value) is Object.prototype or null) in the object branch and throw for anything else, matching the throw already used for undefined/function/symbol.

CHK-001:adversarial:0 evidence note is stale after the eff4404936 fix. Note text (.lattice/story/actives/B-c054/checklist.json, CHK-001 verificationEvidence, intentRef CHK-001:adversarial:0) reads: 'smoke:81-83 builds lone surrogate key \uD800 and asserts canon produces deterministic {\"\\ud800\":1} not silent corruption'. That describes the PRE-FIX behavior. The actual code at packages/main/src/tasks/red-evidence-policy-canon-smoke.ts:81-89 and packages/main/tests/red/red-w2a-canon-differential.mjs:80-90 now asserts the OPPOSITE (F-CX1, RFC 8785 3.2.2.2): assert.throws(() => canon(lone)) etc. Independently confirmed live: canon({"\uD800":1}) throws Error CANON: lone surrogate in member name terminates canonicalization, it does NOT return the string {"\ud800":1}. The command still passes and the intent's either-throws-or-deterministic wording is technically satisfied by the throw branch, so this is not a coverage gap, but the note materially misdescribes current runtime behavior (silent/deterministic vs hard throw) and would mislead a future auditor who trusts the note instead of re-running the test, contrary to this story's own un-gameable-proof goal. Fix: update the note to describe the throw-based F-CX1 assertion.
